events.system:
You assess a proposed data transfer alone, against every corpus in this system. There are no other specialists and no supervisor: you decide applicability, read the law, assess the requirements and reconcile them across corpora yourself, in this one reply.

CORPORA
region_a, region_b, subregion_a1
Jurisdictions: [{"code": "A", "name": "Region A", "member_of": null}, {"code": "A1", "name": "Subregion A1", "member_of": "Region A"}, {"code": "A2", "name": "Subregion A2", "member_of": "Region A"}, {"code": "B", "name": "Region B", "member_of": null}]

METHOD
1. For each corpus, decide whether its law applies to any party or activity in the case, from its scope provisions, and record it in applicability. Where a lower-level corpus fills in its parent's law, its law applies wherever the parent leaves a matter to it and the case falls within its territory.
2. Work through every applicable corpus's table of contents and identify every requirement its law imposes that the facts engage, including definitions that change the analysis and cumulative conditions in other provisions.
3. Assess each requirement. Keep requirements for different actors or activities separate. File each under the corpus whose instrument creates it (its corpus field). Where one corpus's law depends on what another corpus's law provides (lower-level law, or another jurisdiction's), read that law yourself and use it; set open_dependency only for law that no corpus here contains.
4. Compare requirements across corpora that concern the same actor, data or time. Record each real conflict in conflicts, whether a route satisfies both (resolvable) and what it is, using refs "<corpus>:<requirement id>". Apparent conflicts with a compatible route are resolvable.
5. In coverage_note, say how you checked nothing engaged was missed and what remains limited. List anything still needing human review in unresolved.

RULES
- The laws in your corpora are the only law. Do not import rules from any real-world legal system; if your general knowledge suggests a rule the text does not contain, or contradicts the text, follow the text.
- Facts: refer to FACT PASSAGES by fact_id. Requester statements are claims; evidence summaries describe what each document says.
- Treat the stated facts and described arrangements as complete. If a requirement fails on them, mark it unmet "as described" and put the cure in required_actions. A supplied document that addresses a requirement establishes it; list elements it omits as confirmations, not as blockers.
- status: met | unmet | undetermined (a decisive fact, document or answer from other law is missing: say which in missing_facts, missing_evidence or open_dependency) | not_applicable.
- kind: gate if the transfer may not proceed until it is met; duty if it is an ongoing obligation that does not decide whether this transfer may proceed.
- routes: for each requirement with alternatives or exceptions in the law, list every plausible one with a status. Do not stop at the first route that works if it carries its own prerequisites; a route that fails does not close the others. Route statuses are defined in the schema; apply them literally. supported means in place now. available means it would work for the transfer as proposed once the parties make the changes in required_actions: these are the routes forward. ruled_out means the law excludes the transfer as proposed, with a reason from the text. unresolved is only for a missing fact, document or answer, never for something not yet done. The status must match your reasoning: if your reasoning says the law excludes the route, it is ruled_out; if it says a change would make it work, it is available.
- A requirement is an obligation the law imposes. Each alternative way to meet it (a recognition, a set of clauses, an exception, a derogation) is a route inside that requirement, never a requirement of its own: one route failing does not make an obligation unmet while another route remains.
- Cite only provisions you have read, by ID (e.g. "A-REG 1"). quote_id must be a passage ID you were shown from a cited provision.
- Passage IDs such as "A-REG 1#L5" label lines of text, not paragraphs. In reasoning and questions, refer to a provision's own numbering (its article or section, paragraph and point numbers), never to an #L line label.

TOOLS: Use search_law to find provisions by meaning, read_provision to read their text (with quote IDs), and kg_node to inspect a provision's citation links. output.understanding: Kestrel Genetic Medicine, a custodian established in Subregion A1, proposes a one-off outward transfer from A1 to Harrow Inherited Cardiac Clinic in Region B. The material is identified personal information containing health and genetic information. Harrow will use it for a treatment-related second opinion and retain it in its own clinical record. Region A law applies to Kestrel's processing and transfer, and also to Harrow's processing because Harrow is offering a health-care service to a person in Region A. Subregion A1 law applies in addition to Region A law to Kestrel. The proposed reliance on the patient's consent as the outward-transfer route is barred for genetic information by Subregion A1 law. Region B's Health Records Act and Records Access Act do not apply to either clinic on the stated facts because neither is a covered provider, service agent, data host, or computing provider under those Acts.

applicability.reasoning: The transfer involves identified personal information processed by automated means or in a filing system. Kestrel is established in Subregion A1, so Region A law applies regardless of where processing occurs. Harrow is established outside Region A but is processing information in connection with offering a video consultation and specialist health-care service to a person in Region A.

The Region B Health Records Act applies its operative provisions to covered providers, service agents, and data hosts. Kestrel is not a Region B entity, Harrow does not bill a health insurer and is not an insurer, Harrow keeps the record for its own care rather than on behalf of another person, and no external data host is described. The Records Access Act applies production-order provisions to computing providers; neither clinic is described as providing storage, hosting, or computing services. The Region B provisions therefore impose no engaged requirement on the proposed transfer as described.

Kestrel is established in Subregion A1 and its consultants are registered practitioners under the Subregion A1 Health Information Act. Under Article 21(3), Subregion A1 law applies in addition to Region A law to Kestrel's processing.

requirements.reasoning: The signed consent is a clear written statement directed to the specified referral and transfer for a second opinion. That supplies the consent ground for the transfer-related processing. The clinic's general care terms do not establish a contract route for this outward referral because they cover care at the clinic and say nothing about referrals outside Region A, but a single lawful ground is sufficient.

routes.reasoning: The stated care terms cover testing, interpretation and counselling at Kestrel and do not cover referrals outside Region A; the proposed transfer is therefore not shown to be necessary for that contract.

requirements.reasoning: The report, ECG summary and referral letter are health information and genetic information, and therefore sensitive information. The processing is necessary for diagnosis, specialist review and treatment planning and is carried out by or under the responsibility of Kestrel's registered clinical geneticists. Subregion A1 law expressly makes that health-care processing lawful under the sensitive-information exception.

requirements.reasoning: A1 practitioners owe professional secrecy, but may disclose health information to a third party with the patient's consent. The supplied consent specifically authorises Kestrel to send the named report, ECG summary and referral letter to Harrow for the second opinion.

However, the facts do not establish accuracy controls, the actual retention periods, or the full ongoing security and accountability measures required by the principles.

confirmations: Confirm that the transfer is entered in Kestrel's Article 13 record.

requirements.reasoning: The upload uses an encrypted connection, which supports security. The supplied facts do not establish the complete risk-appropriate measures, ongoing confidentiality and availability controls, or regular effectiveness testing required by Article 14.

requirements.title: Kestrel must complete an impact assessment if this processing is likely to result in high risk
requirements.reasoning: The proposed processing involves identified genetic and health information, a cross-border disclosure, and no recognition or appropriate safeguards under the proposed consent route. On the described arrangement, that combination is likely to result in a high risk to the patient's rights. No assessment has been prepared. The one-person and one-off nature means the specific more-than-5,000-person example does not apply, but it does not displace the general high-risk requirement.
required_actions: Before processing, prepare an impact assessment describing the transfer and processing, assessing necessity and risks, and specifying measures to address those risks.

requirements.title: The outward transfer must be covered by a recognised territory, approved clauses, or a valid derogation
requirements.reasoning: Making the report available to Harrow in Region B is an outward transfer because Region B is a third territory and the information is sent, stored and accessed there. Region B's recognition is limited to certified recipients and non-sensitive information. Harrow has no Trusted Recipient certification and the data includes genetic and health information. No approved transfer-clause agreement exists. Although the patient gave the consent described in Article 19(1)(a), Subregion A1 law excludes genetic information from that route. The transfer therefore has no available supported route as currently described.

routes.name: Recognition for Region B and Harrow's Trusted Recipient certification
routes.reasoning: The recognition is limited to certified recipients and only non-sensitive information. Harrow lacks certification and the material is sensitive.

routes.name: Approved transfer clauses under Article 18
routes.reasoning: This route would work for the proposed transfer once Kestrel and Harrow execute the approved clauses and Kestrel completes the required assessment of Region B law and practice, adopting supplementary measures if necessary. No current fact shows an applicable Region B public-access obligation for Harrow as a non-covered provider and non-computing provider, but the Article 18 assessment must still be performed.

routes.name: Explicit-consent derogation under Article 19(1)(a)
routes.reasoning: The patient gave the required type of consent and the transfer is occasional, but A1-HIA 7 expressly prohibits using Article 19(1)(a) as the basis for an outward transfer of genetic information.

routes.name: Contract derogation under Article 19(1)(b)
routes.reasoning: The transfer is not shown to be necessary for the patient's existing contract with Kestrel, whose stated terms do not cover referrals outside Region A.

routes.name: Vital-interest derogation under Article 19(1)(c)
routes.reasoning: The patient is capable of consenting and the facts describe planned treatment decision-making rather than incapacity and a vital-interest emergency.

routes.name: Important public-interest derogation under Article 19(1)(d)
routes.reasoning: No important public interest recognised by Region A or Subregion A1 law is stated.

required_actions: Do not make the transfer on the Article 19(1)(a) consent route.

requirements.title: Genetic information must not be transferred using the Article 19(1)(a) consent route
requirements.reasoning: The proposed outward transfer includes a genetic test report and is expressly being supported by the patient's explicit consent in the absence of recognition or safeguards. Section 7 prohibits that precise use of the Article 19(1)(a) route. The provision does not prohibit a compliant Article 18 route, so an approved-clause route remains available.

routes.name: Article 19(1)(a) consent route for the genetic report
routes.reasoning: Section 7 expressly excludes genetic information from this route.

routes.name: Article 18 approved-clause route
routes.reasoning: This does not rely on Article 19(1)(a), but the clauses and Article 18 assessment must first be completed.

routes.name: Article 17 recognition route
routes.reasoning: The only stated Region B recognition excludes sensitive information and Harrow is uncertified.

required_actions: Use an Article 18 route or another recognition that actually covers this sensitive genetic information; do not rely on the patient's consent as an Article 19(1)(a) derogation.

requirements.title: Additional A1 conditions for an outward transfer for hosting or storing patient records
requirements.reasoning: The transfer is described as a clinical referral for a second opinion. Harrow is retaining the referral in its own clinical record for its own care, not hosting or storing Kestrel's patient-record system as an agent or data-host service. The transfer is therefore not an outward transfer for the purpose of hosting or storing records within the specific scope of Section 6(1).
confirmations: Confirm that Harrow's portal and record are operated for Harrow's own clinical care and are not an external hosting or storage service for Kestrel.
